long_biography.plain_text:
Restaurateur Olivier Bertrand approached the revival of Paris's grand brasseries by widening their appeal beyond tourists. He restored menus spanning affordable dishes and luxury products, alongside service throughout the day. At La Coupole, he found a prewar menu whose extensive selection echoed dishes his restaurants were bringing back. Regular investment in the premises accompanied the changes.

He also used franchising to help employees become business owners. His group supported prospective franchisees with finding a restaurant, arranging finance, setting up the business and overseeing works. The approach offered staff a route from managing someone else's establishment to running their own.
